title: Four native paths in Azure AI Search
brief: Azure AI Search offers four document-level approaches, and three are preview as of 2026-10-13. Choose by where the content lives, how fast permissions must propagate and whether preview is allowed, then label every choice honestly.

blocks.md:
The four approaches are security filters, POSIX-like ACL and RBAC scopes, Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and SharePoint in Microsoft 365 ACLs. Only security filters are GA and work on any API version. The other three need a preview REST API or preview SDK, carry no SLA and are not recommended for production workloads by the docs [[r11]].

A native ACL query passes two checks. The **calling app** needs Search Index Data Reader (or Contributor) through its Authorization header, and the **user's identity** arrives in `x-ms-query-source-authorization`. The service builds the filter itself and a document passes if **any one** of `userIds`, `groupIds` or `rbacScope` matches. Groups, including nested ones, resolve through Microsoft Graph at query time, and if Graph fails the service returns 5xx, never a partial result [[r12]].

blocks.title: The four document-level approaches
blocks.intro: Statuses were checked on 2026-10-13. Freshness always equals the sync path you build.

options.name: Security filters
options.summary: A filterable `Collection(Edm.String)` field plus a filter your code builds with `search.in`.
cons: A string match with no authentication
You write and secure group resolution
options.bestWhen: A custom push index, non-Entra identities, or GA is mandatory.
options.avoidWhen: You do not want to own nested-group logic and preview is acceptable.

options.name: POSIX-like ACL and RBAC scopes
options.summary: Permission fields `userIds`, `groupIds` and `rbacScope`, enforced at query time from the user's token.
pros: ADLS Gen2 and Blob indexers read the permissions, push API covers other sources
cons: Allow lists only, no deny entries
At most 1,000 values per field, one field per type, five rbacScope values
ADLS Gen2 allows 32 ACL entries per file
options.bestWhen: Content in ADLS Gen2 or Blob, or any source whose ACLs you can resolve to Entra object ids, and preview is accepted.
options.avoidWhen: GA only, non-Entra identities, or seconds-level revocation.

options.name: Purview sensitivity labels
options.summary: Labels extracted from Blob, ADLS Gen2, SharePoint and OneLake gate access by classification.
cons: Single tenant, RBAC auth, REST and SDK only
Chunked indexes need the label on every chunk row
options.bestWhen: Classification, not named principals, decides access and labels already exist.
options.avoidWhen: Per-person ACLs, multitenant setups, or you need Suggest.

options.name: SharePoint ACLs
options.summary: The SharePoint indexer ingests permissions with the content.
pros: Inheritance, unique item ACLs, Entra groups
From 2026-05-01-preview: list items, ASPX pages, site groups (`spg:`)
cons: No Anyone or People in your organization links, no guests
An Entra group nested in a SharePoint group is not expanded
Parent scope changes need a resync
Application permissions and Basic tier or higher
options.bestWhen: SharePoint is the source and preview is accepted.
options.avoidWhen: Sharing links or guests drive access, or revocation must beat an indexer run.

blocks.title: Query body, group ids resolved by your code

blocks.md: Nothing authenticates the string. Your code derives the ids from a validated token [[r13]].

blocks.title: Query with the user's token

blocks.md: Store Entra object ids (GUIDs), not UPNs. The special values are `all` (public) and `none`. Without the user token only public documents return [[r15]].

blocks.title: Search POST only

blocks.md: Needs Search Index Data Contributor or a custom role with `Microsoft.Search/searchServices/indexes/contentSecurity/elevatedOperations/read`. It does not work on knowledge base retrieve [[r12]].

blocks.takeaway: GA means security filters. Native ACLs shine for ADLS Gen2 and Blob, the SharePoint indexer for SharePoint with preview accepted, and delegation when seconds-level revocation matters. Say preview out loud.

items.symptom: Results come back unfiltered although the header is sent.
items.cause: An indexed knowledge source was created without `ingestionPermissionOptions`, so the index has no permission metadata.
items.fix: Set it at creation (still preview in 2026-04-01) and verify with a revoked test user [[r17]].

items.symptom: A service-side test with an API key returns only a few documents.
items.cause: Since `2025-11-01-preview` ACL filters apply even with a key or admin role, and a missing token returns public documents only.
items.fix: Send the user token, use elevated read for debugging and re-test anything validated on older previews.

items.symptom: A folder permission change never reaches the index.
items.cause: Parent scope changes are not picked up per indexer run. ADLS Gen2 needs a resync and push ingestion needs a reingest [[r16]].
items.fix: Call `/resync` with `options: ["permissions"]` or `/resetdocs` for SharePoint, resync ADLS, reingest pushed documents and audit drift.

items.symptom: Some users lose documents shared through an Entra group inside a SharePoint group.
items.cause: That nested relationship is not expanded, so the results are filtered out.
items.fix: Grant through supported group relationships or flatten membership at the source.

items.symptom: A few heavily shared files seem to ignore part of their ACL.
items.cause: Entries beyond 32 per ADLS Gen2 file or 1,000 per SharePoint file might not be enforced.
items.fix: Shrink ACLs with groups and flag items above the limit during ingestion.

quiz.q: A test that used an API key and no user token returned about a dozen documents on `2026-08-01-preview`. On an older preview it returned every document. What explains the difference?
options: ACL filters apply even with an API key, and a missing user token returns only public documents
The index lost its permission fields when the API version changed, so the service samples documents
The admin key lacks the Search Index Data Reader role for the index, so results are truncated
Graph was unavailable, so the service returned a partially filtered page
quiz.explain: From `2025-11-01-preview` the filters apply regardless of the credential, and with no token only documents marked public (`all`) match. Earlier previews returned everything for a key or admin role. Losing fields would change the schema, a missing role would fail the call, and Graph failures return 5xx rather than a partial page.

quiz.q: Select every true statement about native ACL enforcement in Azure AI Search (preview as of 2026-10-13).
options: Group membership is resolved through Microsoft Graph at query time, so nested groups work.
A document passes only when userIds, groupIds and rbacScope all match.
If Graph is unavailable the service returns a 5xx instead of a partially filtered result.
The features are GA in the stable `2026-04-01` API.
A document passes if any one of userIds, groupIds or rbacScope matches.
quiz.explain: Filters are applied independently and any match authorizes the document, Graph expands groups at query time and a Graph failure fails closed. The features are not part of the stable 2026-04-01 API, and an all-must-match rule would contradict the any-match behaviour the docs describe.

quiz.q: Match each Azure AI Search approach to a constraint you must plan for.

pairs.r: GA on any API version, but nothing authenticates the string
At most 1,000 values per userIds or groupIds field
An Entra group nested in a SharePoint group is not expanded

quiz.explain: Each approach has a distinct limit: security filters are a plain string match you secure yourself, native ACL fields hold 1,000 values, the SharePoint indexer drops the mixed Entra-in-SharePoint-group relationship and Purview label ingestion rejects user-assigned identities.

quiz.q: A test user without access still sees a file from an indexed SharePoint knowledge source, even with the user token sent. Which change fixes it?
options: Send a token with broader scopes on every query
Set `retrievable: false` on the content field
Use an admin API key so filtering is forced
quiz.explain: Without `ingestionPermissionOptions` at creation the index carries no permission metadata, so the header has nothing to match and results come back unfiltered. Broader scopes and admin keys do not add metadata, and `retrievable: false` only hides a field from responses.

takeaways: Only security filters are GA. Native ACLs, Purview labels and SharePoint ACLs are preview as of 2026-10-13.
Native ACL queries need two checks: the app's role and the user's token. A missing token returns public documents only.
Freshness equals your sync path: SharePoint parent changes need a resync, ADLS needs a resync, push needs a reingest.
Create indexed knowledge sources with `ingestionPermissionOptions` or results come back unfiltered.
Use elevated read to debug, and keep it off the app's normal identity.
